destination.name: Moreton Island
destination.tagline: A sand island of dunes, shipwreck snorkelling and whales off Brisbane
destination.description: Moreton Island is a sand island 36 km long that lies 35 km off Brisbane, and 98% of it is national park. Visitors go for the Tangalooma Wrecks, a cluster of sunken ships that form an artificial reef, and for freshwater lakes, giant dunes and a long surf beach. Cape Moreton has the state's oldest lighthouse, and humpback whales pass offshore on their annual migration.

goodToKnow.title: Ferries run from Brisbane
goodToKnow.detail: Vehicle and passenger ferries sail from the Port of Brisbane, daily in peak periods, and the resort runs passenger services from Pinkenba.

goodToKnow.title: 4WD only
goodToKnow.detail: Only 4WD vehicles can drive the island, and each needs a vehicle access permit.

goodToKnow.title: Book camping ahead
goodToKnow.detail: Camping needs a permit, which must be obtained before you arrive.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Humpback whales pass offshore from {months}, and the weather is mild and dry.
